chapter: New York dance bands and Dorsey
title: Back to the career: Mezzrow's house in the Bronx
summary: Dance steers Freeman back to chronology; he and Floyd O'Brien join Mezzrow's rehearsal band, which does not take off.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: insights into wonderful people and I feel guilty, because I so love to hear you do it, but I must develop you in depth here now.
So all right, you are going to be leaving Chicago now. Now, let's stick with your career and digress just a little bit perhaps with Bix and Jack as we talk and Pee Wee.
Yes, we got the telegram from Mezzrow. I mentioned this earlier. It was forming this black/white band, and of course, we wanted to be in it.

So, Floyd O'Brien and I got on a bus, you know, the trombone player, and came to join Mezzrow. And we stayed, he had a house up in the Bronx, or up near -- yes, the Bronx, I was going to say near Harlem, but it was way up 167th Street, I think, and he had this big apartment where we stayed, we had no money or anything and we were just rehearsing, and Mezzrow was feeding us and what not, and as I say, the thing didn't take, I mean, with all the help of people like Benny Carter and Alex and what not, the thing didn't go and so I got offers to go with other bands.
